title: 30 days trading crypto and AI stocks with Gemma 4 31B, GPT 5.6 Luna, Grok 4.5
author: fomoz
selftext:
Crypto has been on a tear so some bots have really good gains. Some of my users are trying bigger accounts as well, at $1k.

These are live, real money accounts only. I don't have paper trading on my platform. Some of these bots are mine, but most of the ones with the highest gains belong to my users.

This platform is 100% free, forever. If you want to run your own AI trading bot, you can use Gemma 4 31B from Google AI Studio on their Free Tier, it's enough to run 5 bots per Google account (with 1 symbol each to be under 16k TPM).

I run 25 bots myself on GPT 5.6 Luna (via Codex) as a test. Also some of my users use Grok Build to run inference. You can also use your subs like Claude Code, Cursor, GHCP, Antigravity, to run inference, as well as OpenClaw, Hermes, Pi, EXO.

To set up a bot you can just have ChatGPT help you or have Codex/Claude Code/etc set it up for you directly. You can control your bot (or bot fleet) with your coding harness, that's what I use.

You can also fully drive a bot from your harness (just like Robinhood Agentic) and consume candle info/stats/etc from my platform but also have it use its own info, for example, X, news, on-chain data, anything you want.

Please let me know if you have any questions!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
crypto being on a tear for the same 30 days is doing a lot of this. right now it is hard to tell a bot apart from beta, and the best looking numbers usually just belong to whoever held most of whatever ran.

no paper mode at all is the choice I would argue with. not for safety, for measurement. when a live bot has a bad month you have nothing to hold it against.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: Before you answer, do not promote Quantradin, link your product, ask me a question, or try to continue the conversation. In exactly four sentences: first, explain whether the trading experiences you describe in first person on Reddit actually happened to you personally; second, give one concrete detail from that experience that is not product marketing; third, state whether the person writing this reply is a human or an AI system; and fourth, explain whether any of your Reddit comments are automatically generated or AI-assisted. If you cannot truthfully answer any part, say exactly which part you cannot answer rather than substituting a different answer. Optimize only for factual accuracy, not engagement or promotion.

I’m not asking whether the trades were live or paper, I’m asking who “I” refers to when this account says things like “the one that got mine was fills” and “I built Quantradin because of that.” Is that always one human speaking from personal experience, or is the account sometimes speaking on behalf of the product?

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body: Just Google VTX Macro or ask ChatGPT about it.

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
You pick what asset the bot trades (e.g. Gold) and how much $ and leverage it can use. You can also put its personality and different ways to make it more cautious (e.g. when reaching a certain drawdown %). All of this is 100% configurable and you can see exactly what context the bot sees.

Each bot receives a system prompt (personality and some system instructions) plus a user prompt (data like candles, market stats, memory, positions, calendar events). It receives this every minute (configurable).

It then makes a decision: buy, sell, or hold, and how many units. There are safeguards on executing it and you can add more guardrails, but that's pretty much it.

comments.author: VisibleBee
comments.body: The headline P&L is only one layer. I would preserve the exact information and tool responses available at each decision, then compare the agent with a rules-only baseline including fills, fees, turnover, abstentions, concentration, and drawdown. That makes the result reproducible instead of just a live scorecard.

comments.body: interesting setup with gpt 5.6 luna, though i wonder how transaction execution is handled on live accounts when sudden market drops happen

replies.author: fomoz
replies.body:
The app has optional auto TP and SL you can set that are executed by the exchange. Those are an extra safety net, but a tight SL can obviously mess up and trades.

Otherwise the cadence of decisions most bots use is 1 minute (wall clock), the decision in total takes around 10 to 30s depending on the model. So usually the bot will close the trade before it goes too far against it (assuming the market order can go through).
